title: Fixed Assets Accounting and Management
overview: Effective fixed assets management and accounting are crucial for organizations, as these assets are key resources for product production and long-term benefits generation. This course covers the management and accounting of fixed assets based on the British Standards Institute Publicly Available Standard (PAS 55). It introduces the 28 essential points of PAS 55, aimed at maximizing fixed asset utilization. These points are divided into categories: asset policies, strategies, management enablers and controls, implementation of management plans, performance assessments, and improvement through management review. The course spans the entire asset lifecycle, from acquisition or creation to maintenance, utilization, and eventual disposal or renewal.

The accounting component follows IFRS guidelines, specifically IFRS 16 for property, plant, and equipment, and IFRS 38 for intangible assets. Key topics include capitalization rules for fixed and intangible assets, fair value measurement, depreciation methods, and impairment rules, including their measurement and accounting treatment.
audience: This course is designed for professionals involved in fixed asset management, including supervisors, account managers, purchasing and facility coordinators, financial controllers, internal auditors, maintenance managers, and operations managers.
methodology: The course combines consultant-led presentations with participant-led discussions, group exercises, case studies, and role plays to ensure interactive learning.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Implement the 28-point PAS 55 framework to establish a comprehensive asset management system aligned with PAS 55 and ISO 55000 standards
Evaluate fixed asset investments using Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and other financial evaluation tools
Identify and measure fixed and intangible assets according to IFRS standards
Justify the accounting treatment and reporting of assets throughout their lifecycle
Properly account for asset impairment, disposals, and sales of long-lived assets
